messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- Failing test: org.apache.commons.cli.bug.BugCLI252Test.testExactOptionNameMatch()
  - Options defined: long options "prefix" and "prefixplusplus".
  - Input: --prefix
  - Expectation: Parsing should succeed by matching the exact long option "prefix".

- Parse flow:
  - DefaultParser.parse(...) iterates tokens and calls handleToken("--prefix").
  - handleToken detects a long option (startsWith "--") and calls handleLongOption.
  - handleLongOption sees no '=' and calls handleLongOptionWithoutEqual.
  - handleLongOptionWithoutEqual calls Options.getMatchingOptions(token).

- Core issue in Options.getMatchingOptions(String):
  - It strips leading hyphens and then collects all long option names whose names start with the provided string:
    - For input "prefix", both "prefix" and "prefixplusplus" are added because both start with "prefix".
  - If more than one match is found, DefaultParser throws AmbiguousOptionException.
  - Thus, --prefix is reported as ambiguous even though there is an exact match.

- Why this is wrong:
  - The method has a comment “for a perfect match return the single option only” but does not implement an exact-equality shortcut.
  - Correct behavior: If an exact long option name exists, it should be selected immediately and not considered ambiguous, regardless of other options sharing the same prefix.

- Relation to the reported bug (“LongOpt falsely detected as ambiguous”):
  - The bug report’s example (“--import=FILE” ambiguous between "import" and "importToOpen") is the same pattern.
  - For the '=' variant, the parser goes through the with-equals path, but the underlying matching logic still relies on prefix matching and lacks exact-match precedence, leading to the same false ambiguity.

- Conclusion:
  - The failure is caused by Options.getMatchingOptions using a pure prefix match and returning all startsWith matches, without first checking for an exact name match. This leads DefaultParser.handleLongOptionWithoutEqual (and similarly the '=' path) to throw AmbiguousOptionException even when an exact match exists.
  - Implementing exact-match precedence (return only the exact match if present) will satisfy the failing test and fix the reported ambiguity.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
